sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
The window is not a smooth compounder: FY2019 operating income fell 58.9% and operating margin dropped 11.9pp to 8.1% [D97][D109][F23].

That collapse was the $6.8 billion Shave Care goodwill impairment and a $1.6 billion Gillette intangible write-down, driven by currency devaluations, decelerating grooming category growth and tougher US competition [X109][P62].
FY2020 then rebounded with operating income up 186.2% and margin up 14.0pp, $8.3 billion of it the base-period impairment charge, the rest net sales growth and higher gross margin [D148][D160][P71].
In FY2026 non-US sales grew 6.1% and contributed 3.1pp of the 3.3% revenue growth, while US sales grew 0.2% and added 0.1pp [D510][D511][D457][D535][D536].
Net sales rose 3% on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Fabric & Home Care was the largest segment at 34.8% of revenue and added 0.8pp, Beauty added 1.3pp, and Baby, Feminine & Family Care added 0.2pp [D541][D543][D603][D564].
Operating costs grew 2.1pp faster than revenue in FY2026, at cost of revenue growth of 5.3% and SG&A growth of 5.5% [D482][D472][D474].
Diluted EPS grew 1.7% against net income growth of 0.5%, helped by a 1.3% lower diluted share count [D461][D459][D476].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% sat above the 22.1% window median but below the 24.3% FY2025 high and well above the 8.1% FY2019 low [F30][D648][D647][D646].

The 1.6pp margin decline came from a 1.0pp cost-of-revenue effect and a 0.6pp SG&A effect, as gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix and SG&A rose on higher marketing spending [D470][D483][D485][P5].
In FY2026 net margin of 18.4% sat 4.3pp below the 22.7% operating margin, as other non-operating income of $1.1 billion and a 20.8% tax rate partly offset the gap [F50][F30][D693][X108][D443].
That other income rose $922 million mainly on the prior-year Argentina translation charge and the current-year Glad joint venture dissolution gain [P24].

FY2026 operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income, below the 1.25x window median, and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x net income against a 1.02x median [F80][D444][D683][F100][D445][D660].

Operating cash flow rose 10% as net earnings adjusted for non-cash items generated about $19.5 billion, with inventory up $641 million on safety stock and new products and payables adding $919 million [P3].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% was above the 17.2% window median, and capex at 5.1% of revenue was 1.40x D&A [D441][D654][D440][D446].
The company carried net debt of $24.2 billion in FY2026, net cash of -27.8% of revenue, against a -32.3% peer median and a 67th percentile among three peers [D450][D451][D695][D694].
The current ratio of 0.68x was below the 0.72x window median and near the 0.63x FY2023 low, with working capital of -$12.5 billion [F180][D663][D661][F170].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion plus dividends of $10.2 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow, and long-term debt fell 8.6% to $22.8 billion [X134][X144][D453][D468][F190].
Payout at roughly free cash flow leaves little room for a step-up without new borrowing, though the debt reduction in FY2026 offsets that.
The current ratio has been below 1.0x every year of the window, at 0.68x in FY2026 [F180][F171].
This is structural for a consumer staples business funded by supplier payables rather than a liquidity warning, since operating cash flow covers it.
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 at 116.6% and FY2026 at 100.7% [D402][D453].
Two years of payouts at or above free cash flow mean capital return depends on the balance sheet rather than internally generated cash.
Whether operating margin in the FY2027 10-K holds above the 22.1% window median or falls toward the 8.1% FY2019 low [D648][D646].
Whether free cash flow to net income in the FY2027 10-K recovers above the 1.02x window median from 0.94x [D660][D445].
Whether buybacks plus dividends as a share of free cash flow in the FY2027 10-K falls back below the 100.7% FY2026 level [D453].
